subject: zoology
question_text: What are antennae? What is the arthropod group without antennae?

verification.note: Sourced from the Sri Chaitanya Junior Fastrack zoology section (book p.54, VSAQ 102). Zoology holds only ONE source book — the TSBIE Basic Learning Material in hand covers physics only, and no zoology board paper is in the corpus — so the two-book union check and the back-test are both structurally impossible for this card; 'not checked' does NOT mean 'checked and clean'. The mark split is a claim until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: What antennae are
steps.why: The antenna is a head appendage that took up a sensory job, which is why the number of pairs differs from one arthropod class to another.
common_mistakes: Writing that antennae are only for touch. They also carry receptors for smell.
Giving crustaceans one pair. Crustaceans have two pairs.
steps.memory_tip: Antennae are jointed sense organs on the head: touch and smell.
steps.margin_note: What they are and what they do. Two or three lines.
lines: Antennae are the paired, jointed sense organs
borne on the head of an arthropod.
They carry receptors for touch and for smell,
so they are tactile and chemoreceptive.
Insects and myriapods have one pair.
Crustaceans have two pairs, the antennules

steps.label: The group without antennae
steps.why: The name of the subphylum states the answer, because the place an antenna would occupy is already taken by the chelicera.
common_mistakes: Naming Crustacea. Crustaceans have two pairs of antennae, the largest number in the phylum.
Writing 'spiders'. Name the whole group: subphylum Chelicerata.
steps.memory_tip: Chelicerata is named after its first appendage, the chelicera — so there is no antenna.
steps.margin_note: Name the group and give one example. Three lines.
lines: The subphylum Chelicerata has no antennae.
In a chelicerate the first pair of head
appendages is the chelicerae, not antennae.

insider_note: Answering 'spiders' instead of Chelicerata is the common half-answer here — the examiner wants the name of the group.
